text:
name: kitchen_reminder
does: Reminds a person at a chosen time to do a small kitchen job, like taking a warm salad out of the fridge, and lets them update the time later.
inputs: what the reminder is for, and the time or day
people say:
- Tell me at six to get the salad out so it isn't too cold
- Nudge me when the rice should be done
- I keep forgetting the soup, buzz me in twenty minutes
- Can you update my dinner reminder to half past seven?
- Remind me tomorrow morning to buy warm bread

Walt did not trust his phone, but his daughter had left it with him for the trip. "Find me a room in Lisbon for three nights," he told the voice assistant. It showed a long list on the screen. "I can't scroll this thing," Walt said, "read them to me." The signal was weak, so the assistant's voice cut out twice, and Walt stepped closer to the window. The assistant read out three hotels. "The second one," Walt said. Then he stopped. "Wait, no. Two nights, not three. My knees won't take more." The assistant understood that he wanted the same hotel for two nights, so it changed the request and told him the hotel was one kilometer from the station. Walt smiled. "Good. A short walk." He said yes when it asked him to confirm, and the booking was saved.

Grandma Rosa felt sleepy after lunch, but the squeaky door in the back room was driving her mad. "Assistant, please book a repair person for the door hinge on Tuesday," she said. The assistant looked for handymen near her home and found one with a free morning. Rosa was stirring her tea when she remembered her bridge club. "Oh, not Tuesday. Make it Thursday, please." The assistant understood that she wanted the same repair on Thursday instead, so it moved the booking and read it back to her: a handyman would come to fix the hinge in the back room on Thursday at nine. "Good," said Rosa. The assistant also offered to remind her the evening before, and she said yes. Then she finished her tea and took a little nap.

Coffee is the drink many people reach for first thing in the morning. What people change about it is how strong it is and how sweet. Some want a weak cup, some want it extra strong, and a few want no sugar at all. They say things like make it stronger, less milk, one sugar, or a bit sweeter. Some coffee machines connect to the internet, so you can ask for a cup while you are still in bed. A sudden wish for something cold is common too, and then people ask for iced coffee instead. Fruit drinks work the same way. You peel the banana first, and then you can say thicker, thinner, or no ice.

A playlist is a list of songs that play one after another. People use playlists for a walk, for cooking, or to lie on the sofa and relax. What do they change? Mostly the volume, the song and the mood. They say turn it up, a bit quieter, skip this one, play that last song again, or play something cool. When it rains, many people ask for slow songs, and on a sunny day they want faster ones. They can also ask for more songs by the same artist, or say they don't like the song that is playing, and the next one starts. A new playlist is easy to make: say a name, then say the songs to put in it.

A neighbourhood message board helps people who live close to each other share news. Someone has lost a cat, a street party is planned for Saturday, or a band is too loud at night. People use the board to tell the street and to hear back. What they change is who sees the message and when it goes up. They say post this for everyone on the street, send it only to my building, or take my message down, the cat came home. Some neighbours also share a short clip from a wireless doorbell camera. If you have a sore finger and can't type, you can say the message out loud and ask the assistant to post it for you.

name: next_bus_times
does: Tells a person when the next buses or trains leave from a stop and warns about delays.
inputs: the stop or station, the line or direction if there is more than one, and whether they want a round trip home
people say:
- When does the next bus to the library come?
- Is my train running late?
- I don't want to drive today, what is the quickest way downtown?
- Anything leaving Oak Street in the next ten minutes?
- How long until the number 12 gets here?
- I need to be at the airport by nine and back tonight, what should I take?

Marco was making a fruit drink for his daughter's party when he remembered the hot tub. His hands were wet, so he did not touch anything. "Pool pump?" he said to the speaker. The assistant answered that the pump was working and had been running for two hours. "Water heat?" Marco asked. The assistant said the water was thirty-one degrees, warm enough for the kids. Marco split a lemon, turned off the blender so he could hear, and said, "Cover on." The assistant understood he wanted the hot tub cover closed for now, so it closed the cover and told him it was done. It also said the pump would keep running until eight. Marco nodded and went back to his lemons.

Person: I just got home from the night shift and I'm so tired. Can you turn off the porch lights and remind me about the party?
Assistant: Sure, I'll turn off the porch lights. Which party, and what time should I remind you?
Person: The holiday party at my sister's house. Remind me at four.
Assistant: Okay, a reminder at four today for your sister's party. Do you want me to keep the tree lights on?
Person: Yes, keep them on, but I can't stand the constant blinking. Make them steady.
Assistant: I can turn the lights on or off, but I can't change how they blink. That setting is on the lights themselves. I'm sorry.
Person: Fine. Turn them off then. The sky is one big gray cloud and the room is bright enough.
Assistant: Done, the tree lights are off. Sleep well.

name: check_account_access
does: Shows the sum of devices signed in to an account and can sign out the ones the person does not know.
inputs: which account, and which devices to sign out, if any
people say:
- Who else is logged in to my email?
- How many phones are using my shopping account?
- Kick off any device I don't know
- Sign everything out except this phone
- Unpack the whole list of devices for me, I think someone is using my account

name: battery_saver
does: Turns on a mode that makes the phone last longer by dimming the screen and pausing background apps.
inputs: on or off, and optionally the battery level at which to switch on
people say:
- My phone is almost dead, help it last
- Save power please
- Turn on low power when I hit twenty percent
- I have to pick up the kids at six and I only have ten percent left, stretch it
- The smoke alarm app must stay alive all night, make the battery last
- Even with this dirty old charger I want it to hold until tomorrow

Jade was texting from her bed with paint still in her hair. She typed to her phone assistant: "find a video on how to stretch canvas and set a timer for 20 min so the paint can dry". The assistant understood that she had asked for two things. First it searched for a short video about stretching canvas over a wooden frame and opened the top result. Second, it set a timer for twenty minutes. Jade watched the video while eating a juicy orange. When the timer rang, the assistant said, "Twenty minutes are up. Your paint should be dry now." Jade typed "thx" and went back to her painting, a little braver about the canvas.

Priya got home at seven in the morning, tired after a long night on the ward. It was a cold november day and she wanted soup. "What do I have in the fridge?" she asked her kitchen speaker. The assistant listed milk, two carrots, a few eggs and half an onion. "I don't want to go out," said Priya. "And don't order anything big. Just add celery and bread to my shopping list, nothing with nuts." The assistant understood that she wanted only celery and bread on the list and nothing with nuts, so it added those two things, ordered nothing, and said so. Priya said she would enjoy her soup later, and then she went to sleep.

Dan was cooking dinner while the kids ran around the house, and the music was too loud. "Turn the music down by half," he said. The assistant lowered the volume from sixty to thirty. Then Dan said, "Play the dance playlist I saved online." The assistant found the saved playlist in his music account and started it. When the dancing got too wild, he called, "Stop the music for a minute!" and the assistant paused it. "Set a timer for ten minutes of quiet time," Dan added. The assistant set the timer and said so. When it rang, the assistant asked if he wanted the music back, and Dan said yes, at the same quiet volume.

Omar had just moved to a new city, and he did not feel comfortable with the loud beeping from the ceiling. "Excuse me, assistant, I'm very sorry to bother you, but I just moved here from the countryside and there is a beeping noise in my hallway. Could you please tell me whether it is the smoke alarm, and how I can make it stop? I don't want to wake the neighbours," he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to know the cause of the beeping and how to stop it. It said a chirp every minute usually means the alarm battery is low, and it explained how to twist the alarm off its base and put in a new battery that fit. It also offered to remind him to buy batteries before his vacation next week, and Omar said yes.

A bike computer is a small screen on the handlebars. It shows how far you have gone, how fast you are going, and the route ahead. People use it to plan a ride, whether it is a slow ride at the speed of a jog around the park or a big hill climb at the weekend. After the ride, the bike computer and the phone sync, so the ride is saved. Cyclists change the distance, the speed they want to keep, and the route. They say find me a flatter way, add five more kilometres, avoid the main road, or how far have I gone so far?

They want to know the score of the match that is on right now.
What's the score?
Who's winning?
Any goals yet?
Is my team ahead?
The snow knocked out my TV, so I have no idea what is going on with the game.
Did the red team score yet?
My phone says the match should have begun an hour ago, so how is it going?
Could you please tell me the current result of the silver cup final?

Lena ran a small kitchen, and she had just paid for a pricey jar of saffron, the most expensive spice she knew. Late at night she typed fast: "how much did i spned on food this month". The assistant understood the typo, looked at her card spending, and said she had spent 640 dollars on food, 80 dollars more than last month. Lena groaned, then typed, "set a limit of 600 for food next month". The assistant set a monthly food budget of 600 dollars and said it would warn her when she reached 500. That would cheer up her accountant, Lena said, and she turned off the light.

Sam woke up late with messy hair and stared at the dark laptop screen. "Restart the computer and open my files from yesterday," he mumbled. The assistant restarted the laptop, and once it was back on, it opened the folder called Work that he had used the day before. Sam found his document in the middle of the list. Then a message arrived from his friend Ana, who wanted to invite him on a bicycle ride at ten. Sam said, "Tell her yes, and dim the screen, it is too bright." The assistant wrote a short reply that said yes, sent it to Ana, and turned the screen brightness down. Sam rubbed his eyes and started on his coffee.

Tomás was late for class, wearing one glove and holding a stale sandwich. He typed fast: "read this page aloud pls". The assistant began to read the web page in a clear voice. Tomás could not see the small letters well on the bus, so he typed again: "make the text biger". The assistant picked the next size up and made the letters larger. Tomás said it was still too small, so the assistant made them larger once more. He ate the sandwich, listened to the page, and got off at his stop just in time.

People take photos to remember a day. A phone keeps them in an album, and an album is a group of photos, like holidays or the cat. Sharing means sending a photo to a friend. People change which photos go in an album, who can see them, and how big they are. They say put this in the family album, share it with Mum, make a copy, or delete the blurry one. A screenshot is a photo of your screen, handy for saving a thick list or a map. Some phones even listen for your voice, so you can say cheese and the picture is taken.

Person: I need to book movers for our new apartment.
Assistant: Happy to help. What day is the move?
Person: This Saturday. Actually no, my sister can't help on Saturday, so make it Sunday.
Assistant: Sunday, got it. How many rooms need to be packed?
Person: Three bedrooms and a long hallway full of boxes. The kids' teacher said they can miss school on Monday if we need it.
Assistant: Thanks. What is the new address?
Person: 14 Mill Road. We fly out to see Grandma on Tuesday, so it must be done by Monday.
Assistant: Sunday at Mill Road works. I can't pay the movers myself, but I will send the request and you can confirm the price.

They want to move a meeting to a different time without cancelling it.
Move my meeting to Friday.
Push the three o'clock to tomorrow, don't delete it.
Can we do it later instead?
I can't make Tuesday's meeting, find it a new slot.
Shift the team call, but I don't want it on a Monday.
My day is melting, so please slide the review to next week.
The meeting is going in the wrong direction on my calendar, put it after lunch, not before.
Would you mind finding a fresh time for my meeting with Ana? I don't want to cancel it, I only need a different hour.

A meal plan is a list of what you will eat each day this week. People make one so they do not stand in front of the fridge asking what is for dinner. It also helps with shopping, because you only buy what the plan needs. People change the plan for diets, for example low salt, no meat, or more fruit. They say plan my meals for the week, make Tuesday vegetarian, swap the fish for chicken, or I need a packed lunch for my son's swim class. A good assistant will understand what you like and what you don't, and will not give you the same dinner three days in a row.

They want to know what homework is due soon.
What homework do I have?
Anything due tomorrow?
What's due by Friday at noon?
Show me my assignments, please.
I need to know what to hand in this week, like the engine project for science.
Can you cast an eye over my online class page and tell me what is due next week?
Hey, did the teacher put anything new up for tonight?
Could you please tell me which assignments are still open and when each one is due?

Hassan was parked outside a clinic, waiting for his turn. His eyes were tired. A big sneeze made him jump, and then he said, "Read my last message out loud and make the text bigger." The assistant read a message from the garage: the booking for his van was confirmed for Monday at nine. Then it made the text on the phone larger. "That's the minimum I can read," Hassan said, so the assistant went up one more size. He thanked it, put the phone in the holder, and watched the clinic door.

name: door_status_check
does: Tells a person whether the front door and the garage door are locked, and can lock them from far away.
inputs: which door, and whether to lock it
people say:
- Did I lock the front door?
- Is the garage closed?
- I'm at the hotel and can't remember if I shut up the house, please check
- Lock up, we're leaving to stay at Gran's
- It's sunny, so the kids may have left the back door open, is it shut?

Ben had just moved to a new city and wanted to bake bread in his new kitchen. "How long do I bake white bread?" he asked. The assistant said forty minutes at 200 degrees. Ben looked at the stale loaf on the counter and said, "Actually, I want rolls, not a loaf." The assistant understood and changed its answer to twenty minutes for rolls. Ben turned on the oven light to watch and said, "Set a timer for twenty minutes." When the doorbell rang, he said, "Pause the timer," and the assistant paused it. When he came back, he said, "Resume," and the timer started again.

Fatima was making soup when she heard a drip in the west corner of the kitchen. "Excuse me, assistant, could you please help me? I think the pipe under the sink is leaking, and I have a big dinner for forty people tonight, so I need to know if I can still use the water," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted to check her water use for a leak. It said the water meter showed a steady flow even though no tap was on, which usually means a leak. The pot could sit on the stove while she waited. The assistant offered to book a plumber for the afternoon, Fatima said yes, and a plumber was booked for two o'clock.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time without stopping, and then rest. Many people work for twenty-five minutes and then take a five-minute break. It is useful when you have a lot to do or an appointment later and want to use your time well. People change the length of the work time and of the break. They say start a focus timer for thirty minutes, make the break shorter, skip this break, or remind me to stand up. A red light on some timers means work time, and green means break. If you need to pull away early, you can just say stop the timer.

Nia woke up in a hotel room that felt cold, and her phone said it was five in the morning. She could not remember her plan for the day. "Checkout time?" she mumbled. The assistant answered that checkout was at eleven. "Breakfast open?" she asked. The assistant said the hotel restaurant opened at six thirty. "Does that mean I can sleep more?" Nia said. The assistant said yes, and it offered to set an alarm for six. Nia said, "Yes please," and the assistant set the alarm. She pulled the blanket up to her chin and closed her eyes.

Babies eat and sleep on a rhythm, and parents try to remember it. Feeding times are when the baby gets milk, often every three hours. Nap times are when the baby sleeps in the daytime. A baby monitor lets a parent hear or see the baby from another room. Parents change the times, and they say remind me to feed him at two, move the nap to after lunch, play her favorite lullaby, or tell me if she cries. Some parents keep a file on their phone with notes about when the baby ate and slept, and they ask for it before visiting the doctor.

They want the heating turned up.
Heat up the living room.
Make it warmer, please.
Turn the heat up and switch on the radiator in the hall.
I'm bored of wearing three sweaters indoors, so raise it a few degrees.
Put the thermostat up two degrees and turn it back down at ten.
We're going to the cinema at eight, so warm the house before we get back and keep it warm until bedtime.
If the heater is still broken, call a repair person, and meanwhile just set it to twenty-two.
Could you please raise the temperature a little, and also tell me when it reaches twenty-one?

Person: Change password.
Assistant: Sure. Which account, your email or your phone?
Person: My email. I'm new to the city and my old phone number is gone.
Assistant: Okay. I can start the change, but I need to send a code to a number you have now. Can you tell me the new number?
Person: Hold on, I'm hungry and can't think. It's 555 0142.
Assistant: Thank you. I will send a code now. A good new password can be a short sentence with a number in it.
Person: Okay. Can you just tell me my old password?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't. Passwords are kept hidden, even from me. But I can set a new one as soon as you say it.

Person: Take a screenshot of this recipe and send it to my husband.
Assistant: Done, I have the screenshot. Should I send it as a message or by email?
Person: A message. And write "can you buy these" under it.
Assistant: Sent with that note. Anything else?
Person: Yes, put the photos from Lucy's party in a new album and share it with Grandma.
Assistant: I can make the album. Which photos, and from which day?
Person: Saturday's. The kids were calm for once.
Assistant: I found 24 photos from Saturday. I made an album called Lucy's party and sent the link to Grandma.

They want a reminder to take a break while they work.
Remind me to take a break.
Tell me when to rest in half an hour. Actually, make it forty minutes.
Buzz me every hour so I can stretch.
I've been at this desk all week and I care about my back, so nudge me to get up.
Break in 20, no wait, 25 minutes.
I don't want to be rude to the client, so ping me quietly when it's time for a pause.
Please give me a gentle reminder to step away from the screen every hour, if that's not too much trouble.
Pause time at three. No, at four.

A dishwasher cleans dirty plates and glasses while you do something else, like fold the laundry. You put the dishes in, add a tablet, close the door and choose a program. Short programs are quick and use less water, and long ones are better for pots. People change the program, the heat, and the time the machine starts. They say wash on the quick cycle, let it run tonight after ten, use the eco setting, or stop it, I forgot a cup. On a stormy night, people often let the machine run late, because power can cost less then.

Gus owned a small bookshop and was driving to see his sister for the weekend. At a red light he asked his phone, "Is the shop alarm on?" The assistant checked and said the alarm was off. "Turn it on," Gus said. "But I don't want the motion sensor in the back room on, my cat sleeps there." The assistant understood and set the alarm for the front door and the windows, and it left the back room sensor off. It asked him to say his code, and Gus gave the correct one. The assistant said the alarm was on and that it would send him a notice if the front door opened. Gus relaxed and drove on.

Tara was kneading dough with flour on both hands when her son wanted a snack. "Set a timer for one hour for the dough to rise and add yogurt to my shopping list," she called out. The assistant set the timer and put yogurt on the list, and it told her both things were done. Because the dough needed checking, she asked for a reminder each hour, and the assistant gave her an hourly nudge. When the first timer rang, her son came to join her and help shape the rolls. Tara smiled and asked the assistant how long to bake them. It said about twenty minutes.

A kettle boils water fast. You fill it, close the lid, plug it in and press the switch. It stops by itself when the water boils. People use it for tea, soup and instant noodles. What people change is the amount of water and sometimes the heat. Some kettles let you pick 80 degrees for green tea and 100 for black tea. While the water heats, you can dig a mug out of the cupboard. People say boil the kettle, heat it to eighty, keep it warm, or turn it off. A good kettle is quiet, and if it looks dirty inside, a spoon of vinegar helps.

Person: Can you turn off the power to my desk outlet at midnight?
Assistant: Yes. Do you mean every night, or only tonight?
Person: Only tonight. Tomorrow at seven I need it back on, my laptop must charge.
Assistant: Off at midnight tonight and on again tomorrow at seven. Which outlet, the one at the desk or the one by the bed?
Person: The one with the purple tape. I'm a student and my power bill is high.
Assistant: I can switch the smart plug on the desk, but I can't see which outlet has purple tape. Is it the desk plug?
Person: Yes. And can you tap into my bill and tell me what I spent?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't open the energy company's bill. I can show how much power the desk plug used this week.

name: track_delivery
does: Shows where a food order is and how many minutes are left until it arrives.
inputs: the restaurant or the order, if more than one is on the way
people say:
- Where's my food?
- How long until the pizza gets here?
- It's urgent, my guests are hungry and nothing has come yet
- Is the driver close?
- My hobby group meets at seven and the order is late, when will it arrive?
- I want to tweet about this late order, so how late is it exactly?

Mei had just arrived in the city and was holding a bottle of water when her phone rang. She missed the call. "Call back the last number and put it on speaker," she said. The assistant called the number and switched on the speakerphone. It was the landlord, who wanted to estimate the cost of a new lock. After the call Mei said, "Check my voicemail and tell me my monthly phone plan." The assistant played one voicemail from her mother and then read out her plan, which was twenty dollars monthly. Mei thanked it and took a sip of water.

Mr. Hall was not good with technology. He stood by his front door with a bill in one hand and an iron in the other, because the postman was ringing. "Open the door, but do not unlock the back door!" he told the speaker. He felt sad that he had never learned to use the app. The assistant understood that he wanted only the front door unlocked. It unlocked the front door, kept the back door locked, and said so out loud. Mr. Hall took the parcel and said, "Lock it again, please." The assistant locked the front door, and Mr. Hall went back to his ironing.

They want to know when to take their next dose of medicine.
Next dose?
Pill time?
When do I take my medicine?
How long until my next tablet?
I don't want to spend the evening wondering, so tell me when the next dose is due.
My throat feels better after the cherry syrup, when can I have more?
What is the current plan for my pills today?
Please let me know when my next medicine is due, I keep forgetting.

Carl spent his mornings driving a delivery van. Last night he said to his phone, "Tomorrow at seven, tune the radio to the morning news." The assistant understood that he wanted the news station on at seven the next day, and it said it would set that up. The next morning at seven the radio came on. The news said a train had stopped on the bridge and the roads were slow. Carl was glad, because he did not want to pay for a monthly music plan and the radio was free. He took the long way round and arrived in time.

Kai was texting from the sofa when he opened the fridge and found only a jar of mustard. He typed to his phone assistant: "the fridge is empty again lol". The assistant understood that he might want a shopping list, so it asked, "Do you want me to start a list?" Kai said yes: milk, eggs and bread. His mum had left a receipt from the shop on the east side, so he asked the assistant to remind him to visit it after school. The assistant added the three items to the list and set a reminder for four o'clock.

name: bedtime_routine
does: Walks a child through the bedtime steps and plays a short story or a quiet song at the end.
inputs: the child's bedtime, and the steps to include
people say:
- Time for the kids to go to bed
- Start the bedtime routine at eight
- Tell Mia it's time to bathe and brush her teeth
- Read a short story to the little one
- Play quiet songs on the radio until she falls asleep
- Make bedtime half an hour earlier on school nights

Zoe was texting on the bus: "table for 4 tomorrow at seven at luigi's pls". The assistant understood that she wanted a table for four people at Luigi's tomorrow evening at seven, and it made the booking. Then Zoe asked, "do they have fast takeaway too?" The assistant said Luigi's did takeaway and that most orders took about fifteen minutes. Her friends wanted something to chill with, so she asked about cold drinks. The assistant said the menu had juice and soda, and a liter of lemonade for the table. Zoe sent a thumbs up and put her phone away.

A clock tells you what time it is where you are. A world clock tells you the time in other places, which is useful when you call a friend far away. When you travel, the time zone changes, and so the clock changes too. Some people pick the time zone by hand, and others let the phone do it. People change the city, the way the time is shown, and whether it is twelve or twenty-four hour time. They say what time is it in Tokyo, show me London time, or switch to the twenty-four hour clock. A pencil mark on a paper chart can help, but the phone's setting is permanent until you change it.
